Romans 1 24 Wherefore God also Gave them Up to Uncleanness through the lust of their Own heart to dishonour their own bodies, between themselves One Thing Wherein the Xtian Appears to be more Excellent and better suted to the End of Religio than Any other in the World is the the Punishment of sin that it threatens is far more dread not only the Reward Reward of holiness is Greater and Infinitely more Excellent. but that the Punishment of sin also that it threatens.. is more dreadfull. and thereby is h holy more Gloriously declares the Justice of God. and honours his holiness and his Law but t tends more effectually bring men off from a wicked life to Walk in Which has such a horrible Puni Eterna Punishment affixed to us it. And it wonderfully unfolds those tidings which were so difficult and Perplexing to men before Even Gods Dispensations in his Providence towards Wicked men in suffering to live and Prosper in the World, it shows us the Justice of God in so dealing with sinners and that instead of its 'being from Gods injustice or Unmind fullness of their wickedness that it is Part of their Punishment. and that the most dreadfull too in its Consequencies to obstinate sinners Rom 9 22 What if God Willing to show his Wrath and to Make his Power known Endured with much long suffering the Vessels of Wrath fitted to destruction And by our text also we may be instructed in the Reasons of Gods suffering & Letting men alone in their sin The Apostle is here speaking of the Inexcuseableness[^004-note1] of the heathen Yea altho they had no light but the light of Nature to teach thei Go by. and how God was Provoked by them and stirred up in his Anger stirred up Against them. in that Even they who Are in so Great darkness sinned agais their light. inasmuch as they might know much of God by the book of the Creatures tho not by the book of the Scriptures, 18 19 . & 20 verses

## 29. Rom. 12:18 29.Rom. 12'18 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Romans 12 18 if it be Possible as Much as lieth in you live Peaceably with all men This Chapter is a sort of a summary, of those virtues and Graces of f Amiable actions, and heavenly dispositions which more especially adorn the Xtian, And shine brighter than other men, if the Rules of this Chapter were but followed Universally in the World it would make most surprizingly tranform it and alter it and make it anothe in Comparison but little differing from Jerusalem v. 1 abov the Chapter is well worth Our most diligent and frequent reading and that we should bind the words. and Rules thereof that we should bind them Upon Our hearts. yea that they should be written in indelible Characters there, that it should be the object of Continual meditation lying down & Rising Up and that we should frequently Examine Our lives by it, as by an excellent Catalogue of those those Duties and Practises which if Performed will make us Appear Xtians indeed, and will war mould our hearts and Regulate our lives According to the Jesus X and his image. if this Chapter were but eyed and so put in Practise by us we should excell, 1 in those du lively true devotion. in disposi tions and duties more immediately Respecting God, which Are here most livelily Represented. and Powerfully Urged verse 1.2 I beseech you therefore brethren by the mercies of God that Ye Present Your bodies a living sacrifice, holy acceptable Unto God which is Your Reasonable service And be not Conformed to this World but be Ye transformed by the Renewing of Your mind that Ye may Prove what is that Good and acceptable and Perfect will of God & vrse 11 not slothfull in business fervent in spirit serving the Lord. 2 here Are Perfect Rules which if followed will make us excell in the duties more immediately Ref Relating to Our selves verse 3 for I say through the Grace Given to me to Every man that is Among You not to think of him self more highly than he ought to think but to think soberly according as God hath dealt to Every man the measure of faith, & verse 12 Rejoicing in hope Patient in [^005-note1] tribulation. but more Especially 3 here Are directions for behaviour with Relation unto men which which do t exceedingly tend to make man kind happy, and to make each Particular Person, both excellent & blessed wi in human & Xtian society, and Every Particular society to flourish and Prosper, from the 4 verse to the 8 here Are Rules how to behave Our selves in Our Particular stations. Among, and duties from thence Arising incumbent On us from the 4 verse to the 8 and then the duties which are Undistinguished ly incumbent Upon all towards Each other. as from the 9 verses 9 & 10 Let love be Without dissimulation Abhor that Which is Evil Cleave to that Which is Good be kindly affectioned One to Another with brotherly love in honour Preferring One Another. and from the 13 verse to the End. here we Are Exhorted to Distribute to the necessity of saints, and to G be Given to hospitality to bless them by Whom We are Ronged and abused. to bless alwaies and never to Curse. to simpathize with others either in their prosperity or adversity from love to them And When and to Rejoice with those that do Rejoi ce and weep with those that weep as if their Prosperity were Our Own. we this is not only our friends but if we would be as Xtians we must Rejoice at the happiness of those that Persecute us. and weep and be Grieved for their misfortunes. here we Are Exhorted to Unamity and to be of the same mind one towards Another. not to mind high things but to Condescend to men of low degree those that Are below Our selves and not to be wise in our Own to Recompense to no man Evil for Evil, & to provide things honest in the sight of Conceit if these things were but followed. What follows in the next verse the verse of Our text Would of Course follow. if men did use themselves to be kind Unto those that Abused them, and to bless those those that Perse cuted them. and did not mind high things but were hum ble and lowly and would Consdescend One to Another. and were not wise in their Own Conceits. Pe there would need be no more in order to Obtain Peace i with all men [^005-note2] if men we that is if they were tenacious of their Own Opinions, and as thinking themselves wiser than any other If men were slower in Resenting injuries . and would never Recompense Evil for Evil. and would be fair. & Open and sincere in all their dealings, and honest in the sight of the World there would need no more in order to Obtaining peace with all men. That which follows this verse seem to be Directions by What means we shall thus obtain Peace with all men Dearly beloved avenge not your selves, But Gi Rather Give Place unto wrath, f if we would maintain peace we must not avenge our selves and Go About violently to Resist What is done in Opposition to Our selves. no but we must Give Place to wrath for God has Challenged vengeance as his Own Prerogative. Therefore if Our Enemies hunger we Are to feed him if he thirst we must Give him drink s this is all the Revenge that we must Use make Use of of we must not be Overcome of evil but Overcome evil With Good.

## 32. Ps. 119:60(a) 32.Ps. 119'60 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Ps 119 60 I made hast and delayed not to keep thy Commandments when we find holy and Righteous men in the Scriptures solemnly making Profession before God of any thing in them selves, as pleading as an instance and argument of their Integrity. or as praising God for Granting them such a disposition, or Enabling them to do such actions; It is the same thing to us as if we were directly Instructed in Our own duty. and such Professions are to have the force of Commands with us. Therefore when the Psalmist says I thought on my ways and turned my feet unto thy testimonies. I made hast and delayed not to keep thy Command ments. It is the same thing as to Every one of us as if he had said think on thy ways and turn thy feet into Gods testimonies make hast and delay not to keep Gods Commandments. Here we may observe

______________

1 the substance of this Profession of the Psalmist is his obedience and observation of Gods law. the living accor ding to that Revelation which God had made of himself which is is perhaps more Plainly implied in the foregoing verse by that Expression I turned my feet into thy testimonies by meaning the by Gods testimonies that testification or Revelation which God had made of himself & his will

______

By keeping Gods Commandments is to be understood the whole of Religion both in its Inclinations and actions. its habits and exercises both internal and external. all in heart and life that appertains to Godliness is more frequently in the new testament Represented by the mo names of its internal exercises of faith and Charity f Charity and the like. which in the old is Called keep ing the Commandments of God being more Agreable to the Imperfect state of the Church under the law of moses 2 we may Observe the Circumstance of Time & [^008-note1] manner of his Thus doing. he did it speedily and immediately he made hast and delayed not he thought on his ways, as he says in the foregoing verse he Considerd his his life and actions and wherin he found his ways were wrong he immediately Rectified them the first thing he did was to Repent and Reform he saw the evil of his and stay'd not to allow himself a little further Gratification of his sloth or sinfull desires. he staid not till. this or that d business was done but without Any hesitation or delay betook himself to his duty The Words Therefore Teach us this do

------------------------------------------------------------

Doc That we ought to make Religion our Present and immediate business The Proposition is so Evident of it self that a proof would be needless if it be Our duty to Obey Gods Com mands tis our duty to do it without delay for while we delay to Obey hi them we disobey them. Gods Commands in the t La Commands in the mean time are neglected where he Gives no Indulgence.

__________________________

However that Our sense of our Obligations to this may be lively. and that we may see the aggravations of the Contrary may be neglect may be seen we shall Illustrate Endeavour to Illustrate the truth of the Doc by the following Considerations.

____________________________________________________

1. It appears that we Ought to make Religion our present and immediate business because tis the business for which we Came into the world God Raised us out of the dust of the Earth for this End. for this he his hand. formed these Curious frames of our bodies. & breath into the habitation so Prepared these Understanding and Immortal Souls. our being set Above the beasts of the Earth by a power of Reason and Reflexion, and [^008-note2] our being mad Rulers over them. and Possessors of this Low er World is in vain Without thir. we might have served to Inferiour Purposes as well If we had been made sheep. If were not for this there would have been no need of at the of Introducing this animal in the Image of God at the End of the six days works and Our Very beings are in vain without Religion and if we are Created for this End we live in vain as long as we delay or Put off this business served for this end that we may have opportunity for this business Tis for this End that the sun dayly arises upon us that the Rain descends and that the Earth brings forth for us. and for which. the beasts all the brute Creatures with which the [-] Earth the sea and the Firmament of heaven is filled. are are subservient to us. for this End our breath was Given to us at first and for that our vitals are still kept playing surely then we Ought not to for Any time to neglect or at all to delay this business seeing that whilst we so do we live in vain and do but Cumber the Earth the to no purpose the Candle of life burns in vain we Eat and Drink and our heart beats and our blood Runs. the machin wears and the Inf the Wheel wears out at the Cirs Cistern and we Gradually draw near to the Grave and in the mean do nothing of that which we were made for as long as we neglect this business which is Our main End however we may otherwise Employ our selves we spend our time unprofitably for all other business is subjected to and subordinated by God to this because all the Inferiour ends of our being or subordinated to the Chief end are good only as they have Regard to that highest End. whatever business men Employ themselves exercise themselves in yet if they dont bring forth the fruits of Righteousness they are look'd upon by God as barren trees and Cumberers of the Ground Luke 13,7

__________________________________________________________

2 Religion is a business infinitely the most excellent and of the Greatest importance. Tis what the Common sense of all men dictates. that things of the Greatest importance should be first take Care of, Because the neglect of them may Prove of greater [^008-note3] because the neglect of obst -------------------- the Utmost that Any other employment or exercise Respects is this World Our stat , that is Considerd abstractedly as a worldly Employment and having no Regard to Religion . it affects us only while we stay here, Let that be a longer or a shorter time If we obtain any happine Good by the Pursuit of it. it Can Cost us no longer and Perhaps not near or the Cost or damage that we Can sustain through its neglect Can Cost us no longer, and Perhaps not near so long as we live here. yea of the Event is very uncertain whether we shall obtain these worldly ends that we propose or no by it. or whether or no the Event would be quite Contrary to w our desires and expectations But the least that the Business of Religion has Respect to is an Eternity from the pros Eternal misery Ensues from the neglect of it and Everlasting happiness from the speedy and diligent pursuit. If we through delay should happen to lose our opportunity as it very often happens than there is no help or Reme dy but that we must be Everlastingly miserable & ou no Repentance or tears or after labours will avail us any thing, either to the obtaining of that eternal Good that we had an opportunity of obtaining If we had timely improved it, or for Our deliverance from, or the least mitigation of that torment that we suffer Now tis as Certain as Any thing Can be the least misery that is Everlasting is more dreadfull than the Great est that has an End. and that tis our twould be our Prudence to pursue the least happiness that we Shall never be Deprived of, than to neglect it for the Greatest that in we are Certain of In a short of losing. but the [^008-note4] misery that we avoid and the happiness that is attaind by Godliness is not only infinitely exceeding that wch is Earthly in d its Continuance but in its Degree & wi heigbht, as the afflictio Losses and afflictions of time are to be dispised in Comparison of damnation because they are but for a few moments, so they are As nothing in when Compared with those flames or as to Greatness of torment. If it Can be supposed which that which yet Cant be allow'd that we shall for the Present shall in be less happy for in neglecting the world for the sake of Religion yet in a few years it makes no add, we shall not be never the worse for it, but are sure of being the better for it forever, and surely tis a point of Prudence to undergo alittle short inconvenience for the sake of a lasting happiness. Good and furthermore if Let our Circumstances be what they will we are not sure of being the worse for it while we are here, yea we have Great Reason to Expect to be happier even in this world. but if we dont enjoy more of the world we are sure of having more Peace and Contentment in what we do Enjoy, which is better than abun dance However, had not we better Run the venture of suffering a little here of foregoing some sensual outward delight than of usff of missing of heaven. or of suffering a little s for the Present than of Enduring a Gods wrath alwaies. if If we miss our opportunity we are sur misery this is sure to us and if we hear Gods voice to day while its Calld to day we are sur t and diligently as the work the work of God happiness forever is sure as the word and oath of God

________________________________________________________

3. It appears that we Ought not for any time to delay or put off Religion because all our time is Gods. we Our selves are his he has made us and Given us [^008-note5] all our powers of action and all the while we Refuse delay the work of Religion we unjustly keep from him that which is his due and which he most Just ly Challenges of us. all the while we live he preserves our life and he Requires that that life whi which he upholds should be immediately devoted to him he Gives us our power of thinking, and and we Cannot. think a thought without him and surely our thoughts ought all w al he Gives o Preserves our powers of acting and tis in him we live move and and surely our thoughts and actions ought therefore immediately to be Given to him. we have not one moment of time but what O is God Gifts to us in his han if we procrastinate Religion till to morrow that the next year this year is as till another season we in the mean time Rob God, for this year is his as well as the next. if we are preserved live till that time, it will be because God feeds us, and Clothes us till then. tis Gods wool and flax his Corn his wine and oil that sustains us while we live in sin against him. Hosea 2 8,9 for she did not know if I Gave her her Corn and oil and multiplied her silver and God which they prepared for Baal. there fore will I Return and take away my Corn in the time thereof and my wine in the season therof & will Recover my wool and my flax

____________________________________

4 by Delaying Religion till another season Great Contempt, is Cast on Gods Authority. It becomes up us when we Recieve Commands from those that Are our Rulers, and very much our superiors, not only to obey exactly but immedi forthwith and without delay. that we may show the Cheerfullness and readiness of our Obedience. but how provoking is it when the Omnipotent almighty God himself Commands for man, for worm us that are not worthy to be his servants to be slow in obeying. Especial [^008-note6] ly when Expresly requires present and immediate immediate Obedience. when God says now for the sinner to say not now but when I have a more Convenient Opportunity. When I have more leisure from my own business, and when I find a Greater disposition to it than I do now. When God says to day while it is Called to day, to delay for whole weeks, months, and years. & the Excuse is that there are other things to mind. or he feels very much Indisposed to such thing as God Commands. he dont love the work that God sets him about. Is not this Enough Greatly to incense Gods Displeasure, & to Rouse his Justice, and bring down his wrath in peals of thunder upon such, Especially Considering that Gods Commands are so much inculcated and acco panied with promises and threatenings as well as Gracious invitations and Intreaties. and fatherly Correc tio . what Prince will bear this of a subject or what master would bear it in a servant. yea what a Prudent parent would bear it in a Child.

______________________________________________________

5 In delaying U Religio Putting of Religion we manifest a Great Slight of Gods Glory and excellency. hereby God is set last and in the lowest Place as if he were least of any thing to be Regarded; his business must be done Last, as if it were no Great matter whether it were ever done at all. and other things were much more to be Regarded than bein he. This is the Language of their Practice: God has his demands tis true. but I have this world and my own appetites, have their demands too. & God must wait wait till they are served first and Even sin and Satan must have their share before God. so the sinner Puts satan on Gods Right and Every filthy Lust [^008-note7] and desire must be serv'd before him. and Every Creature is exalted above the C Creatour. and the high & mighty and mighty God must be in the Rear of all

such Contempt as this those that delay to keep O Gods Commandments do most Certainly Cast upon God; they delay to hearken to God for the Sake of their Ease their sinfull and sensual Pleasure sensual and sinfull Plea sures. Placing God lowest in their affections and last as to times. Giving the sin and the world their Youth their strength and the bloom of their life. he God must be turn'd off with old age. with decripit Years a & a decayed mind and body and must Even E'en take up with that or have none at all. Or perhaps only a little time upon their death beds, when the frame is breaking to Pieces and they taking their leave of the world then they would devote themselves to God and live to him malac 1 8 and if ye offer the when life is no longer their own blind for sacrifice is it not evil and if ye offer the lame and the sick is it not Evil offer it now unto thy Governour -------------------------------------will he be Pleased with thee or accept thy Person saith the Lord of hosts 6 Delaying to keep Gods Commandments is the Greatest Abuse of Gods Pati mercy and Patience. to what an abuse is it, because we Read of that God is Gracious and mercifull long suffering. slow to Anger, to take occasion from thence to dare to Go On in sin against him. to disobey dishonour and affront him because he is mercifull, because he is a Gracious being that is willing upon Repentance to forgive our faults; this is to do what in us lies to Render unto God Evil for Good, and to be the more his Enemy because he is inclined to pity and help us. how ungratefull is this. if we did not hope that God is so mercifull a being that he would heart us and pity tho we we do allow our selves to sin against him and provoke him for some time longer, we dare not God on in sin with such freedom, we should fear his wrath and anger, and should be more Carefull; but this is that which Encourages men [^008-note8] they think that Prayers and tears will do as well afterward as now. and so they Give themselves a liberty. but how ungratefull is this. This in scripture is Called despising Gods Goodness . Rom 2 4 or despisest thou the Riches of his Goodness and forbearance. and longsuffering not knowing that the Goodness of God Leadeth thee to Repentance.

There was the same also the same Usage and upon a better foundation in that nation that was Gods peculiar People and the Only nation of all Upon the face of the Earth that Professed the true Religion and upon a better foundation even the divine appointment who had their solemn sacrifices was their Custom by divine Appointment to offer up their Cattle first fruits of their Land. their Gift their Corn their silver and Gold . their wine and their oil and their Cattle which were dead sacrifices But the sacrifice here Enjoind is the sacrifice of our selves [^009-note2]

all to be fruitless and vain & they are as much in as much danger and distress as ever they were the dreadfull sound still follows them & all their Refuges dont Prove Sufficient to Give Rest to their souls thus they are weary with wandring to and from fro & they are weary with striving to Procure Rest for themselves II Enq. what it is to Come to X for Rest. here are these three things 1 . The soul is made sensible that there is Rest to be had in X . the sou soul thus Burdn'd & weary is very sensible of its need of Rest . & it has been seeking of Rest in other things & thought to have found Rest in them he hoped to find Rest sometimes in this thing & sometimes in that but now he is very sensible that no Rest is to be found in them . but he now sees where Rest is to be had. he is Convinced that there he may have Rest in X. he was burdend with a sense of his Guilt he sees that in X he shall be free from Guilt that if it be in him he shall be deliver'd from that Burden . he was Burdend with fear of wrath but he sees if that in X he shall be free from wrath safe from that wrath . X has made satisfaction to offended Justice & has made a his satisfaction is sufficient . he sees a way how G. may the wrong done to Gods majesty & may be made up th so that he may be saved & that not be Injured he sees in X enough to satisfy the Craving & needs of his soul 2. he Chooses & desires Rest in X . he Chooses Xs Rest that Rest that X Purchased for him & that he offers to him. he had Rather have that Rest than Rest in the 0 or worldly Good things . the unbeliev which is a holy & heavenly Rest a Rest of Complacency in G. & in his Gracious Perfection a bearing X yoke & doing his work. he Chooses Rest in Xs way above all other ways [^009-note10] that he Can think of he Chooses it Rather than his ow safety & Rest In X Righ. & by hi in the Grace of G. in him Rather than in his own Righ he delights in that way that Gives so much Glory to free Grace he Chooses his Rest should be attributed to X that all the glory of it should be Given to him. [ ] 3 . he that Comes to X for Rest appli the soul applies to X for Rest it seeks it of him his application is to him & his expectation from him . he Committs himself to X that he may Save him & Give him Peace he Looks to him as they that looked to the brazen serpent in the wilderness & were healed. III X will surely Give Rest to all such weary & Burdend souls that thus Come to him. 1. if they Come to him he'll take away that which was their Burthen. and will secure them from that which they feard. X has undertaken to save take the Guilt of such upon himself that he will be Responsible for them that their debt shall be Put to his account & that he will secure them from the wrath which they fear . this is the work & Business which he has undertaken . he Engaged to do it before the foundation of the 0 even from all Eternity he has undertaken to be the Refuge & saviour of all those that are afraid of Gods wrath that Come to him. & X has Promised it t faithfully Promised it to men he has Plighted his faith for their security if they Put their trust in him . he hath thus done by his own free & voluntary act . if sinners if sinners Come to X tho they have done that whereby they have exposed themselves to Gods wrath & to the stroke of Justice it it or it is not their Concern how they shall satisfy or how they shall Answer for what they have done it is X Con X looks[^009-note11] upon it as his Concern he'll look to that. Let there be never so much wrath deserved they if they are in X they are as safe as if they never had deserved any because X has undertaken to stand in their stead Let there be more or Less There need be no fear whether his surety ship will be accepted of the F upon their account for he is Chosen & appointed of the F to this very work. tis the F. that sent him into the T , X obe died & suffered wrath in obedience to the F. & There need be no doubt of the sufficiency of what X has done for he ful has fulfilled the Law the Law is as so much fulfilled by hi as if they themselves Per had Personally obeyed or had Personally sufferd the Curse of the Law. & then Gods honour wont suffer at all by their escaping Punishmt & being made happy. for what X has suffer'd has Repaired Gods honour & what he has suffer done has done much more honoured G. than ever our sins dishonoured him. so They need not doubt of finding acceptance with the F through the son seeing that X is so dear to G. a Person that is Intimitely near to him & in whom he is Inf initely delighted. 2. X will Give sensible Peace & Rest to their minds in a sense of the Removal of their Guilt & their sufering from Punishmt. there shall be more or less of a sense of this here in this T X Give Peace of Conscience to believers tho it may be much Interupted as in this Present state as faith itself is but where there are exercise of faith there a will be more of or Less of this Peace. & Generally X Gives to believers mani manifestations of his Gods favour & love that are exceeding sweet & Refreshing & very much Quiet & Compose the mind in a sweet Rest & Calm . this is that Peace that X Gives Joh 14. 27 Peace I leave with you my Peace I Give unto you not as the T[^009-note12] Giveth Give I unto you . Let not your heart be troubled neither Let it be afraid This is the Peace of G. that Passeth all understanding Philip. 4. 7. and however this Peace may be Interrupted in this world as the exercises of faith are Interup and if their Peace be much Interrupted in this T tis evermore through want of faith tis because their faith is weak & Interupted tis because they dont Come to X so often and trust in him so fully & so Constantly as they ought to do & however this Peace may be Interupted with doubts & fears in this T . yet hereafter it will be Perfect & undisturbed forever. this everlasting Rest will Jesus the true Joshua Give to all those that Come to him for Rest . Heb. 4. 8. 9. Applicat The Improvemt I. shall make of this is to Invite those that are thus weary & Burdend to Come to X you are sensible that you are in a dole full Condition that is dismal to Go about having Gods wrath Impending over your head not knowing how soon it will fall upon you . hanging over the Pit by a slender thread not knowing Every moment but that you may drop in . it is dolefull if we Consider the turmoil & uneasiness that such a Condition Causes in is attended or may Just ly be attended with this life . & you have some experience of it You find nothing but wearisom days & wearisom nights your heart is filled with fears & you have n little or no Comfort in the T your Burden is so Great that you are Ready to Cry out under it . you are weary of it and how heedless it is that you should Continue in such a Condition when X offers you safe ty & Rest freely .[^009-note13] how happy would your Condition be to what it now is if your heart were but Persuaded to Close with J. X then you would be out free from Guilt & out of all danger. whatever storms were without you might hear the Rush of the Rushing of the wind & the Roaring of the thunder while you are Quiet & safe in a safe shelter. O be Persuaded therefore to Come to X, that sufficient that blessed & excellent saviour that was wear Laboured & was heavy Laden for our sakes under the heavy wrath of G. so that we who had Committed the sin might have safety Ease & Rest forever [^009-note14]

Rev 14 18 19 And Another Angel Came out from the Altar which had Power over fire And Cried with a Loud Cry to him that had the Sharp sickle saying Thrust in thy sharp sickle and Gather the Clusters of the vine of the Earth, for her Grapes Are fully Ripe. And the An gel thrust in his sickle into the Earth and Gathered the vine of the Earth and Cast it into the Great winepress of the wrath of God The Things that Are spoken of in this Part of the vision. of John do seem to Relate to the beginning of those and introduction of those times so Often prophecied of in Scripture, wherin the kingdom of God shall be set up through the world and the king dom of the devil destroyed and the Interest of iniquity overthrown, wherin God by wonderfully signal mercies shall advance and bless his People and wherin he will inflict sore and dreadfull Judgments on his & Thire his Peoples Enemies This seems most Probable by the order and pla and depen dance of the Chapter in the foregoing Chap we had an Account of the Power and dominion of Antichrist the Beast that all thew world wandered after and then in the Beginning of this an Account of those holy Ones who withstood all those temptations and kept Pure from spiritual defilements whie while all the world besides was adulterated and followed the Beast instead of following the Lamb as from the first to the 5 verse. And from the 6 verse we have An Account of the Renewed spreading of Gods kingdom and the Revival of the truth in the World. after the Great apostacy of the Church and the Uncontrouled Power of the beast And I saw Another Angel fly in the midst of heaven having the Everlasting Gospel to Preach to them who dwell on the Earth and to Every Nation And kindred & [^010-note1] tongue and People &c- And then we have an Account after this of the Gathering in the Elect of God into his Chh the Great harvest of the world which is when there shall be such a wonderfull flocking of men to Jesus Christ And the full time shall Come and all things shall be Ready for the designed ingathering of the Nations to the mount Zion 14 verse and I Looked and behold a white Cloud ----------------------------

If the Decalogue was at their disposal we shall should not have ten Commandments. if the Bible were to Come Under their hands we should have it much Lessend, some Yield external obedience to some of Gods Commands for Interest, others for Credit others to Appease the Rage of their Consciences foolishly Entertaining a hope that God will be Pacified. with Respect to their Neglect of some duties for their strict observance of others Yea men will do almost any thing Rather than Come to this universal Obedience and wholly Cut themselves off forever from all the Enjoyments of sin from Every dear lust, and deny themselves Perpetually the Gratification of Every sinfull Appetite and wholly spit out the dear Morsel without any hope, or Expectation of ever tasting it Again. they subject themselves to Severe fastings. and Abstinence from the Common Comforts of life, and seclude themselves from human society. will undertake Long Pilgrimages & part with all their outward Goods, will severely macerate and put to pain their own bodies, Rather than Part with all their sins an There Are many that would Compound with God and say as Naaman did. 2 kings 5 17 18 shall not then I Pray thee be Given to thy servant two mules burden. of Earth for thy servant will henceforth, offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice unto Any other God but unto the Lord in this thing the Lord Pardon thy servant that when my master Goeth into the house of Rimmon to worship there and he leaneth on my hand and I bow my self in the house of Rimmon, when I bow down my self in [^011-note32] the house of Rimmon the Lord Pardon they servant in this thing. Naaman was Convinced that the God of Israel was the only true God being so miraculously Cured of his Leprosie as we may see in the 15 verse behold now I know that there is no God in all the Earth but In Israel. But yet it being the Custom of his master and his Countrey to worship in the house of Rimmon and it would be Contrary to his Interest and honour to neglect it he desires to be Excused in that one thing. so many men

_____________

so many men will observe some Commands yet there are Particular darling sins. that they will allow them selves in. and hope to make Up the matter by a strict observance of other Commands. some men may allow themselves in the Enjoyment of some lust and hope to make amends for it by a strict and devout attendance on family Religion. Others are Constant attendants on Publick worship and Put on a Religious mask in Gods house, that nevertheless may allow themselves in intemperance and excess. How many think to Attone for a neglect of the duties of the second table by a strict observance of the Externals of the first. and on the Contrary how many seem to think that God will be a Peace with them as to their neglect of the duties of the first table that Respect God for their honesty and Uprightness and Generosity towards men. But how contrary is this to universal holiness. and aliene from Xtian Obedience how far are these from being truly holy as God is holy in all manner of Conversation When it is thus it is a thus it is a sure token that we they sin was never truly mortified in them. for it lives and prevails and has Dominion over the heart still in some instances which it Could Never be if it were truly mortified. for when Once the fountain is Dried Dried up all the streams fail, when once the head is mortified [^011-note33] all the members Perish. when once a mortal blow is Given. at the Root all the branches wither and the Continuing of one known sin is as sure an token of the life sins being alive still in the heart as if they were all Continued, as the Continuing of one vital facul ty or power in is a sure sign that the body is yet alive when men bent seem to be Religious but bent universally so it is a sure sign that their Religion is for self-Ends that the principle of their Obedience is something Else besides a Love to God and a Gracious Respect to him. for that would make them study Labour to Please and obey him in all things. and fear to offend him in any thing

If he has Chosen God for & his Law for his Whole Portion why dont he keep Close to him why is he not satisfyed without the Any Enjoyments that he has forbidden. but tis Evident that notwithstanding all his Pretences he has a Reserve in his own breast for something Else that he Chooses for his Portion

III Use Exhortation. Let us be exhorted to be holy in all manner of Conversation. If we Are not so Our high priviledges which we Enjoy, our having the way of salvation Declared to us, and life and immortality brought to light and heaven brought so near to our view. our having having so Clear a discovery of God and Jesus X and such Glori ous del Declarations of Grace in the Gospel will all Instead of being of advantage to us will turn to our Condemnatione Turks and heathens will Rise up in Judgment Against us that we may be Perswaded to that holiness which is Universal. Let us Consider the following things

________________________

1 that Gods Eye is Continually upon us. & his Eye is too Pure to bare bear iniquity to iniquity, he searches and tries our hearts and Our lives, and sees us wherever his Eyes follows us wherever we God. and sees wherever we hide Our selves. the If we pretend to be holy and are strict in many things Yet if we Retain any sin and harbour any lust. he takes notice of it and knows it altogether and writes it down in his book, and there [^011-note34] 'twill stand as an article against us and will effectually bar us from his favour and he will hold us Enemies till we forsake it and tho we ma men may make many excuses for their sins and Plead what Great temptations they lie under. and how hard the Contrary Duty is how Contrary to their Interest and may Plead necessity. but will not be so mocked but will Certainly Require it of them

_______________________________________________________

2 Consider that Except our holiness be Universal we Cant exspect the Comforts of a Godly life. Great are the Consolations and Spiritual Pleasures which the truly Godly Generally Recieve here ' Enough to Pay for all their Pains & labour. and more than Enough, that is the Reward of Godliness that is Given in this life and which the such Comforts are what the saints have Great need of in this weary Pilgrimage. and sometimes they are so Great that they Are Unspeakable and far exceed all other Comforts and Pleasures upon Earth. But Except we are universally holy tho we may take a Great deal of Pains in Religion and very much deny our selves but we shall miss of all the Joys and Peace and Joy of Godliness.

those sins that Are Retained will be Separation wall between God and us and will obstruct the light of his Countenance and hinder all Communion and manifestation of Divine love and favour. it will hinder peaceo one allowed sin is Enough to hinder all peace of Conscience and Cause wos and tumults in the mind and excite fears and dre to hinder all assurance of a Good Estate and excite fears of and horrors and fears of wrath and to make a dreadfull sound within in a hi within his Ears the sinners Ears

there may Indeed be a false Peace and false Comfort but that is not life the true tis but as a pleasing Dream which vanishes forever when he awakes. tis as Ever as the Prophet says Isai 29 8 as when a hungry man dreameth and behold he Eateth but he awaketh and his soul [^011-note35] is Empty

3 Let us Consider that if the allowing our selves in the neglect of any Dut one duty or the Commission of any sin will Greatly disadvantage us in doing our Duty in other things. the Commission of that sin. keeps the whole body of sin alive in the heart. and Continually feeds nourishes and stro Corruption. and arms and strengthens that mortal Enemy which men have in their own breasts. the Committing of one sin Reno the allowed Commission of one sin Greatly Upholds and Increases an Inclination to sin in General, and the wilfull neglect of one duty begets an indisposedness to all Duty. we shall find that it will be as fetters and Chains and a Continual Pull back to us and will Endanger our Relapsing into Universal wick a total hardness of heart and stupidness of mind. and our Carelessness and neglect of all Gods Commands and an Universal breach of them and Constant breach of them

4 & Lastly Let us Consider that Notwithstanding all Pretences to faith that we must at Last be Judged by our according to Our works. when we Are Are Called forth at the Great day to Appear before X to be Judged it will be Enquired what we have done. and they whose faith hand hant been fruitfull in a holy a holy life their faith wont save em, James 2. 14 What doth if profit my brethren tho a man say he hath faith and have not works Can faith save him. we have it abundantly declared to us in the Scripture that we must be Judged according to Our works. where we have the day of Judgment Particularly described in the 25 of Math beginning with the 25 verse it is not said what habits of fa Grace they had but what works they Did. Let none therefore Encourage themselves from any hopes they may have from their Experiences to neglect holiness of life for we the verily of tho Grace be wholly wrought by the spirit of God yet tis not what has been wrought in the heart but what has been wrought by the heart that we must be Judged by Let us therefore follow after holiness without which [^011-note36] no man shall see God. and Let our holiness be exercised in all manner of Conversation. Let us keep all the Commandments of God with Care and diligence and have Respect to God in all we do. When we Converse with God alone in the duties of secret worship. Let it be done in the most sincere and holy manner we Are Capable of in the Exercise of all the Graces holy Graces of faith. hope and Love humiliation. Repentance and Confidence

& when we Come together to worship in Gods Sanctuary Let Each of us Do Our Part that there may be holiness in our assemblies. alwaies wor serving God in the Beauties of holiness, that God may delight to be Amongst us and in the midst of us. that we may have the Father and the Son Dwelling with us. Delighting to walk amongst us as in his Garden of Pleasant fruits and when we Converse one with another Let Our Conversation savour of heaven. Let it appear to bystanders and those who Are witnesses of Our behavior that we Are Persons that have been with God. and have Conversed in heaven and Learn'd of X that others that behold of us may say of us verily these Are the Children of the most high If we Are Xtians Let our Conversation with Each others be the Conversation of Xtians. Xtians Are a Generation that Are not of the world and have very little to Do with the world in Comparison of their Other Concernmts, and why then should not their Conversation at least sometimes be about their Business . All sorts of men are most apt to speak of those things that Pertain to their business thus seamen will talk of the sea and seafaring matters. the husbandmen of things Relating to husbandry. and scholars of books and why not Xtians of X whose Name is as ointment poured forth Let us behave Our selves holily in whatever business we [^011-note37] are Conversant & Let there be nothing that is holy nothing that is honourable nothing that is Lovely but what is Pursued by us as becomes those Who Are Called by so holy a God and are United to the holy Jesus Let us Practice whatsoever things Are true. honest, Just Pure, lovely, of Good Report virtuous or praise worthy

Let us keep Close to God in all his Ways and Obey him whatever he Commands and if it Comes to that that we must follow Cut off a Right hand or Pluck out a Right Eye Let us not unworthily Shift our Duty and Put if off either totally or Out of its proper season Let us never say to X Go thy way for this time. when I have a more Convenient season Ill send for thee Let us follow the Lord Jesus wheresoever he Goes which is Given as the Character of the true followers of X Rev 14 4 here Let us Avoid two very frequent Errors of men Concerning the Nature of holiness if we would attain to this Universal holiness of life

1 Let us not Place the Whole of Religion in an Observance of the duties of Instituted worship. such as strictly observing and sanctifying the Lords day, Constant and devout attendance on the Publick worship, and Preaching of the Word or Observing family and Closet duties, in Reading the holy scriptures and other books of devotion these Are Certainly very Essential Parts of Religion but there Are other things of as Great Importance which many seem to think but the Clothing of Religion. such as humility. Patience. temperance mercy and Peace Charity brotherly kindess and a hearty seeking our Neighbours welfare. these are Essential to holiness and no Less so than the An Attendance on those Institutions. and are as much Insisted on in the word of God yea God has told us he will have mercy & [^011-note38] not sacrifice Tis as much holiness to help our brother who needs our help as it is to be Constant in secret Prayer, there is as much Religion in forgiving an Injury as in devoutly attending on the duties of divine worship see what a description the apostle Gives of true and holy Religion James 1 21 Pure Religion and Undefiled before God and the Father is this to visit the Fatherless and widows in their affliction and to keep him self unspotted from the world

2 Let us not Place too much Religion in External actions either either- of the first or second table either in diligently attending outward Institutions of worship or in outward acts of Justice temperance &c neglecting faith Repentance, Love and Joy in the holy Ghost, & the new Creature which are the ry life and soul of Religion without which all the other things are nothing but the body without the spirit, nothing Can be more Plain and Evident yn this; for what are External Actions of a Reasonable Creature Considerd without Regard to the Principle whence they flow more than the actions of a clock or mere ma machine Even men will not Accept the external actions if they suspect the Principle a man will not accept the outward kindness of Another if he Suspects it proceeds not from a Real Good will. how then Can we expe that God will delight in any of our Actions when at the same time he knows them not to be done from any true Regard to him

## 37. John 15:5(a) 37.John15'5a trans

Jonathan Edwards

John 15 5 I am the vine Ye are the branches These Words were spoken by our Lord Just before his Passion after he had filled their hearts with sorrow by telling of them that he was Going to Leave them As to his bodily Presence that he should for the Present be with them no more he Going where they Could not follow him

_____________________

These Are that Part of his farewell discourse to them his Last Words that he uttered to them upon this occasion that being full of Grief were as so many Children hanging about their dear Departing Father & he says many things to them both by way Consolation & Counsel & Concludes all by Praying with them and for them as in the 17 Chap

________________________

He told them by way of Consolation that altho he was Going away for the Present but would not Leave them alwaies but in due time would Return to them again that he only went to Prepare a place for them in his Fathers mansions and in due time would Return to them Again and take them to himself . and that in the mean time he would not leave him Comfortless but would send them a Comforter as in the 16 17 18 & 21 Chap of the foregoing Chap

___________

He tells them What adversities an Contempt an Reproaches and Persecutions they must expect in the world when he was Gone and Gives them Counsel how to behave themselves in such Circumstances. And is Parti cularly Carefull of their steadfastness & Constancy if in this faith and Profession of his name and Obedience to his Commands and as an argument to Persuade them same, Purpose he sets before them their Absolute depen dance upon him for all Spiritual and Least in the midst of the many Persecutions and trials they should meet with when he had Left them they should him & the Gospel of his Grace as an argument & motive to their steadfastness he sets before them their Absolute dependance Upon him for the life of there souls and the necessity of Continuing in him in order to their bringing forth fruit and being acceptable to God. Which he [^012-note1] Illustrates by the similitude of a vine and branches Possibly occasion'd by the Appearance of a vine in the way from Jerusalem to mount olivet which it seems they were now walking Our Saviour Resembles himself to the Root and stock of the vine from whence all the branches Recieve their sap & life by which they bear fruit. The similitude is much of the same nature as others in the SS whereby X is Called the true olive Resembled to the Root and of the olive and stock of the olive tree and we as branches Grafted in. X to the head and believers as members of the body that Recieve their that Recieve their life and are Actuated by him and by which X is and by which he is Compared to a tree of life or a River of water of life & the like

These Doc two doctrines are included in the Words The doc That X Jesus is the true original and fountain of all Spiritual life and nourishment

Tis Implied & supposed in the doctrine I That believers are Spiritually United Unto Jesus there as the branches are united to the vine nor can they derive nourishment from is a Spiritual Union between X and believers. such a it except they be united to it union that they may be look'd Upon as. of There is that change and alteration in the soul of the believer and that they are so united to X, and there is that that Passes between X and them and such a Relation betwixt them that in Gods account they Are One. and and Scripture account they are one and they are the faithfull are Look'd on by X Jesus as one with him self In that Ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren Ye have done it unto me says X in the 25 of math 40 verse The Union is such that X is their its Compared with the Union of the son with the Father Joh 14 20 I Am in my Father and you in me and I in You and 17 21 22 23---------------------------------------------------- [^012-note2]

we have already mention'd those Comparisons by which believers are Called his body Ephes 5 30 for we Are members of his body of his flesh and of his bones. 1 Cor 6 17 for he that is Joyn Joined to the Lord is one Spirit

II Believers derive from X all their Spiritual life and nou rishment. in these two Respects is X Jesus the fountain of Spiritual life and nourishment. 1. as he is the Author of the Outward means of of Spiritual life and nourishment 2 as he is the immediate Source & fountain of Spiritual life it Self. But First He is the Author of all the means of the Spiri tual life. Christ having freely, and of his own Gracious inclination undertaken the Salvation of men Redempti on of men and it being Covenanted between him and the Fa ther from all Eternity that he should be the Author of Eternal Salvation to the Elect. God the Father has committed all affairs Relating to it, and the Whole Care & Government of his Church more immediately unto him. he is the Great medium of Communication between heaven and Earth. God is treating with mankind in a new Covenant and he has Committed the Disposition of things Relating to it and the management of our Salvation by it to his son. and tis from him nextly that we have Recieved the means of Eternal life. 'twas by him as that God was wont to Reveal himself of old. it seems to have been the Second Person in the trinity yt appeard to moses in the Bush & from time to time. and that manifested himself to the Congregation in the wilderness. And the same Person that manifested his Person Presence in ye temple and tabernacle. And that it was the same that orderd the affairs of [^012-note3] the Church of Israel that Presides in the Xtian Church the same that dwell'd between the Cherubims that afterward tabernacled with man in the flesh. And it seems that the Communication between God the & the Church from the beginning of the world has not been immediate but through the son John 1 18 no man hath seen God at any time the only begotten which is in the bosom of the Father he hath declared him.itsThe Son of God whose delights are with the sons of men who all along dwell'd with them and yet Dwells with his Church in the execution of his kingly office It is by X that we have the word of God. Yea he himself is called the Word of God as in the 1 Chap of Joh 1 verse and in the first epis of Joh 1 Chap 1 v & Rev 19 13 he is the Eternal original word, of whom the written word and the holy Scriptures, and the word Preach'd is but an Emanation. the from him. The ministers of the Gospel are his messengers and Ambassadours, from him yy have their mission, him they Represent and to him they are accountable the ordinances of Religion they are all from him he ordaind and Instituted them

____________________________________________________________

Secondly he is the only fountain of the internal life and nourishment of the Soul it it self . Which Consists in 3 things Three things 1 Spiritual knowledge 2ly Gracious inclinations 4 Spiritual Comforts and Refreshments. and Lastly of the Perfection of these in Glory

__________

1 he is the fountain of Spiritual knowledge. tis his office to teach and Instruct us in divine things, he Came down from heaven to turn men from darkness unto light to Let us into the knowledge of those things that the dark benighted world (however they Are what above all things Concern mankind are Yet) without him above all thing ignorant of man in his fallen state he knows Least of all about his maker and will be Ignorant till taught by X. Math 11 27 all things are delivered Unto me of [^012-note4] my Father and no man knoweth the son but the Father neither knoweth any man the Father but the son and him to Whomsoever the Son will Reveal him. because There is a Spiritual knowledge and divine know ledge which they that Are Spiritually alive have which they that have no Spiritual life Are as destitute of as one that is naturally dead is destitute of natural knowledge. There is a seeing and discerning the truth and excellency of Divine things which a natural man (however he may Give a General Assent to things that we Are told of as Doctrines of Religion, that there is a God. & that the Scriptures are his Word & Such like) knows nothing at all of This knowledge and Spiritual understanding may Properly be Called the nourishment of the Soul. the mind of man is nourished by knowledge. it as it were its food

whereby it Gets Strength and is Refreshed as the body is By food. Knowledge in General may be accounted the nourishment of the mind but more especially that which is Spiritual, tis a more excellent Substantial &

sweetest sort of food to the soul than any other insomuch that a man that is fed by it Shall never hunger or thirst more now Tis from our Lord Jesus X that we Recieve this aliment and food of the mind he feeds us with this as the sheep people of his Pasture and the Sheep of his hand. Tis because X is the Original of this spiritual light that he is called the sun of Righteousness. a star what arises out of Jacob a light to lighten the Gentiles. John 12 46 I am Come a light into the world Whosoever believeth on me shall not abide in darkness 2 X Jesus is the fountain of all Gracious Inclinations [^012-note5] and affections. the Soul Cr X is full of Grace him self and God the Father hath Given him the Spirit without measure. in him dwell all the fullness of the God head. and all the excellencies and Perfections of the Father are substantially Copied in him and he is a bright and Perfect expression of all his Glory . So he Communicates of his Infinite fullness to believers and all that holiness and Grace they have is derived from him & they Are his Image and Reflexion Joh 6 57 I live by the Father so he that Eateth Me Even he shall live by me & 14 20 at that day ye shall know that I am in the Father and You in me and I in You.

____________________________________

The souls of believers the Elect are Committed to X and he adorns them those Gracious dispositions that heavenly and divine temper whereby they soar above the vanities of the World and are conversant with angels and the souls of Just men made Perfect and with God the Glorious king of heaven and Earth. He Gives Grace in Regeneration Gives a new principle of life and action and he increases Grace: believers after they are Convicted are still as dependant on X for the exercise and Growth of Grace as for the first bestowment the exercise of it is more lively or more frequent and the growth of Grace Greater or less according to the his Good Pleasure in the dispensation of the Riches of his Grace.

_______________

3 4 tis by X assistance and Influence that men live well and bring forth the fruits of Righteousness. of our selves we have no strength to think a Good thought or speak a Good word or to do Any thing that shall be acceptable to God. all the Exercises of Grace all holy actions depend as much upon X Jesus as the Actions of the body or members do upon the Influence of the Soul. we Are as branches that Can bear no fruit except by virtue of the sap that is supplyed from the vine, as in our text and Context, abide in me and I in you as the [^012-note6] branch cannot bear fruit of its self---------------------

______________________________________________________

--------our living well so much depend on the Influence of X that the Apostle says not I live but X livith in me Gal 2 20

4 4 He is the Original of all Spiritual Refreshment & Consolation. one End and effect of the nourishment and food of the body is to Refresh and Renew it to Enliven the Spirits X is the source of that nourishment by which the soul is Refresh'd and Comforted. Here only Can any that are weary and heavy Laden with sin and spiritua Remorse of Conscience, and fears of wrath, find Rest and here. and here Only Can We find Any true Rest from the troubles from the afflictions and adversities of the world

This life is a weary Pilgrimage full of so many difficulties, troubles Crosses, & disappointments, that except we have Comfort from Placee it is enough to tire out such a poor weak and frail thing as man is : now there is no Resting Place to be found in the things of this world tis an Uneasy and an Uneven World and there is nothing Earthly in which we Can find a little Respit. It is all as a flood of waters Unstable and inconstant if we set our foot on it and would Rest our selves upon it it sinks under us. so that like the dove that Noah sent out we Can find no Rest for the Soul of our foot except we Come to X Jesus, the only Ark where we Can Safely set our feet, and have a shelter from the wearisom storms and tempests of this world. There's none of those that Enjoy most of the World and of the Comforts of it Can say they Ever found a satisfying Rest in Any of these things. If we fly to Riches and hope to find Rest there, we shall sink instead of that we shall probably find an increase of Uneasiness. As the Countreys that have the Richer mines have the frequentest Earthquakes so the minds of those that Possess the most Gold and silver [^012-note7] have Commonly the most frequent Disturbances and Perplexities. Riches instead of Refreshing the Weary is like to make them more weary and as he that Carries the b a Great burthen tho it be of Gold is m sooner weary than he that Carries but Enough to bear his Charges. instead of satisfying the hungry and thirsty it doth but enflame the Painfull appetite eccles 5 10 he that loveth silver shall not be satisfyed with silver nor he that loveth abun dance with increase. I If we fly to honour hoping to find Rest there satisfaction there we Shall find an increase of fear and danger. those that Are exalted high, have Less Quiet & safety, and are in more fears of a fall than those who Are in a lower Station

_____________________________________

If we trust to Earthly friends hoping for satisfying Com fort in them we Shall find them as beautifull Spectres that vanish while we Are Embracing them, they are not able, Compleat to fill the desires of the mind. If we try all Earthly things and after the Example of the foolish Children of Men Wander from one thing to Another we may Spend our whole lives in seeking Rest and finding none. so tempestuous and stormy so shadowy and vain is this uncertain & Changeable is this world that there is nothing to be found that will Give Any Rest to or satisfaction to the Poor weary hungry souls of the sons of men

___________________________________

But if we Go to X there we shall find Rest. there and there alone we may be Easy there we may be shelterd from all danger tempests and disturbances however Great there we may sit down after we Are tired and weary & spent and Rest without Any disturbance or uneasiness. There we may Lay our selves down and sleep sweetly and Quietly the Lord sustaining of us. after we have been wearied by temporal affliction or Spiritual trouble and the weight of our sins we may safely Repose our head on X bosom and there we shall find Respit. Math [^012-note8] 11 28 Come Unto me all Ye that Are Weary and heavy Laden and I will Give You Rest

________________________________

He has indeed appointed every event all things that happen more from all Eternity but in some things he makes his appointment and influence. more evident and Conspicuous. by such an ordering and Guidance of Providence that there should be les is less appearance of dependence on a Constant Course of Second Causes so that man should neither by his Reason. be Possibly able to foresee the Event. as he may many other things which altho they are appointed by God Yet are nextly Produced by ordinary and known natural Cau ses. and also so that man should not be able by his own Endeavours with the Exercise of all his wisdom and Power to determine or alter the Event it God determines many other things that Yet for their Production in the Ordinary Course of Providence depend on mans Power and designation because God has appointed to bring them to Pass by those means. but death is so determind by God and what he Reserves to his own more visible and Remarkeable disposal. that the Event does not so much depend on mans appointment or the exercise of his Power or skill or any other visible second Causes. and

Indeed all other things Comes to Pass by divine providence as well as this. but in this he makes his Providence more obvious and visible Not but that mens lives and health are often Preserved and lengthen'd out by Prudence, Care, and temperance God Rewards those things with health and long life and they have also a natural tendency to Produce This effect. but Yet the Particular time of mens death or the Continuance of their lives are not so Constantly dependent on those or any other means that men Can use. that it may be said that tis is mans Power to Continue, his own life. or that he Can have any Certainty as to its Continuance God is wont to make his interposition and Providence more appa apparent in such Events as are of Greater Concern and moment. When he leaves others of less impor tance to a Constant Course of natural Causes. thus, we are taught by the scripture that the affairs of kingdoms and of Wars between nations are said to subj are subject tho to the special ordering of Gods providence. it is said that he Removeth kings and setteth up kings. and the hearts of kings are in the hands of the Lord and he turneth them as the Rivers of water. he is said to be the Lord of hosts. because he Especially interposes in battles

Psalm 147 1. And Praise is Comely. David was a person that spent his life very much in Gods Praises. he was an excellent musician and excell'd all in the Land in musick and Poetry. & as such was Chosen by Saul before Any other to Relieve him in his dark Gloomy, and melancho ly frames and to drive away the Evil Spirit by whose Influence his mind was so darken'd and ter rified. Saul Gave Command that the best Mu sician. the Cunningest Player in all the Land should be brought 1 Samuel 16 17 18. And saul said Unto his servants provide me Now a man that Can Play Well and bring him Unto me then Answer'd One of the servants behold I have seen a son of Jesse the Bethlehemite that is Cunning in Playing &c and 23 verse. And it Came to Pass when the Evil Spirit from the Lord was upon Saul that David took a harp And Played with his hand so Saul was Refreshed and was well and the Evil Spirit departed from him

2 God is to be Praised for his Goodness. Not but Gods Goodness his essential Goodness is Part of his Greatness as it is a Divine Perfection. but Yet when God is Praised[^014-note7] for his Goodness to us he is not Praised for it meerly as it is a perfection of his Nature. but as it is exerted towards us and we Are the Objects of it. so that it is a different kind of Praise is that which is Called thansgiving. It is Indeed very Proper an for us when we have experienced the mercy of God, and praise him for that at the same time to Praise him for his other perfections We are Called upon by the Goodness of God to take notice of all his Attributes and to be affected with Every Excellency of our benefactor.

## 40. Luke 9:23(a) 40.Luke 9'23a trans

Jonathan Edwards

Luke 9 23 And he said Unto them all if Any man will Come after me Let him deny himself and take up his Cross daily and follow me . Gal 2 20 X having Given a wonderfull manifestation of his Pow er and Evidence of his being some emi Extraordinary Person. by feeding and satisfying five thousand men with five loaves and two fishes. he took Occasion to ask his Disciples what people thought of him. who they thought he was that they saw Did such wonder work such miracles and did such wonderfull things and upon their Answering him that some thought he was John the Baptist, others Elias and others one of the Antient prophets Risen Again he proceeds to ask them who they thought he was. for it seems the People tho they were so various in their Opinions Concerning. none or very few of them thought Right of him. Peter who alwaies seem'd the most forward and Con fident on such occasions answers the X of God without hesitation the X of God X according to his divine wisdom Used to take such Opportunities wh to tell his disciples of his sufferings that he was Undergo, when they were prepared for it by seeing of him work some signal miracle and wonderfull Evidence of his being the Messiah when they Could best bear it. and such news would be the Less likely to shock their faith thus he did after they had been surpriz'd by the Glory of his transfigura tion. as in the 9 Chap of Mark at the 12 v. so now after the working this miracle of feeding such a multitude with so small a matter. seeing them so well assured he let them know that he whom they followed as being the messiah that from the beginning of the world had been prophecied of and who they saw do such wonderfull works should be Rejected of the Elders and Chief Priests & scribes and be slain and Raised the T third day verse 22 which was what they little Expected would befall the X of God. for the disciples tho [^015-note1] they were true saints and those whom X had Chosen to be Especially with him, to be witnesses of what he did and sufferd and to be Late first and principal Instruments of setting Up his Kingdom in the world. Yet they were hitherto very Ignorant Relating in many things Relating. to X sufferings and the nature of his Kingdom and the manner of his Redeeming the world. And had Entertaind the same Apprehensions Concerning the messiah as the Rest of the Jews that he was to Reign in Great Earthly Glory. and thought because they were his followers and disciples they Expected Great advancement too. But But says X X took all opportunities to Get them from those notions & prejudices. and in this having told them of his own sufferings he tells them that they must likewise suffer and must expect no other if they would follow him than to be deny themselves and after his example to bear the Cross

Which we shall more particularly explain Under this doctrine. together with the neccessity of it Under this doc Doc That If we Would be X Disciples it is Necessary[^015-note2] that we should Deny our selves

If an Injury is Aggravated at all in any proportion whatsoever by the merit and excellency of the person Injured, it will most surely follow that that offence that is Committed against a person of Infinite excellency is Infinitely aggravated. it is Certain and without dispute that if an affront Injury [^021-note21] to an excellent person deserves more. and an Injury to a more excellent Person deserves a Greater Punishment & for that Reason because he is more excellent. then an Injury & of Abuse to A Infinite person deserves a Person One of Infinite excellency and Glory, deserves an Infinitely Greater Punishment than any Injury to a finite Person for that Reason because he is a being of Infinitely Greater excellency the Consequence Certainly is very Clear.

Jan.56. 1. upon the fasts for the Earthquake Jonah 3 10 And God saw their works that they turned from their Evil way and God Repented of the Evil that he had said he would do Unto them and he did it not we have here an account of Gods mercy to an heathen people that were Got to a Great degree of wickedness and tho their sin was so Great that the Cry of it Came up before God Yet God before he destroyed them was willing to Give them warning of it that they migh. have opportunity of Reforming that there might be a possibility of their Escape. he therefore sent Jonah to warn them of it. 1 Ch 2v Arise Go to Nineve that Great City and Cry Against for their wickedness is Come Up before me when Jonah after he Endeavoured to Avoid the mi doing of Gods Errand and was swaol swallowed by a Whale and vomited upon Dry Land. when he Came to the City and declared that in fourty days Nineve should be destroyed they were mightily Awakened by it they believed it God and Proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth from the Greatest of them Even to the Least of them. and the king of nineve upon the News of it. Arose from his throne and Put off his Robe from him and put on sackcloth and sat in ashes and Caused it to be Proclaimed through Nineve [^022-note1] by the Decree of the king and his Nobles that no Creature neither man nor beast should tast Any thing neither meat nor drink for three days and should all be Covered with sackcloth and should Cry mightily to God. and Every one turn from his Evil way and from the violence that is in their hands. for Who Can tell say they but that God will turn and Repent and turn from his fierce Anger that they perish not

Math 6 33 But seek ye first the kingdom of God and his Righteousness and all these things shall be added unto You. The drift of What the Chap from the 19 verse to the is to war in this X in this Part of his sermon from the 19 verse of this Chap is warning his hearers against Earthly mindedness and exhorting to heavenly mindedness. he exhorts us not to Lay up treasures on Earth but in heaven. and not but In heaven not to take thought be taken up with Cares which will presently fade away. but to Lay up treasure in heaven that will never fade, he tells us that we Cant serve God and mammon if we are servants of this world we Cannot be the servants of God its impossible to be worldliminded and heavenly minded both at the same time. he exhorts not to suffer our minds to be taken up with Cares and though about meat and drink and Raiment but Rather to Care for our lives and our bodies which we shall loose if we Car w by having both soul and body Cast into hell if wi dont Care for for if we have our minds only taken up about these things and neglect our salvation and Least we should make this excuse that we Cant live in we have need of these things and Cant do without 'em and that therefore there is a necessity of taking Care about them thought for them X takes off this objection by Referring telling of them the Instances of the fowels of the Air how they Are fed and the lilies of the field how they Are Clothed without any thought Cares of theirs though they were Creatures for Just things of so much Less Consequence than man and if God Can feed and [^024-note1] Cloth them so he Can us a without taking thought so he Can us. and he is not Ignorant of our wants for he knows that we have need of these things as well as we our selves.

## 51. 51.Luke 2'14a trans

Jonathan Edwards

Luke 2 14 - And on Earth Peace The Angels sing the different effects Glorious effects of X taking on him the human Nature first in heaven and then on Earth In heaven additional Glory to God. to Give Glory to God had been the Employment of that World from the beginning. & that is the He 1 and Gods Glory is Continually manifested there in a degree and manner inconcievable to us who dwell on Earth. but Yet this was a new manifestation of it to them even to them and Gave them a new theme of Praise the Effect of it which th on Earth Which they Celebrate is Peace. Peace was Gone from the Earth Ever since the fall and Enmity and Confusion an had Reigned in this Lo Lower World they sing sing of the Prospect of the Restoration of a

_____________________________

By Peace oftentimes in scripture is intended Good or Welfare in General. thus Peace be With You was a Common salutation. signifying a desire of their welfare. It seems there to be Intended in a more proper and Restrain'd sense and happiness in the General to be Intended Rather in the Last Clause of the Verse It was Prophecied of the kingdom of the messiah that it would be a kingdom of Great Peace and as if his Coming should Cause war and Contention to Cease from the Earth and the Wolf should dwell with the Lamb. and the Leopard should lie down with the Kid. and the Calf & the Young lion and the Fatling together. and that Nation should not lift up sword against Nation nor Learn War any more. that is that the nature of the Gospel and Kindom of the messiah. should be Peacefull and tending to nothing but Quiet and tranquility. & so far as Embraced and Practiced should Utterly Rec Destroy and Quell the Contrary Evils. and make this Lower World Like heaven in that Respect. where Peac has its Uninterrupted kingdom. X Coming added the E did as it were add this Earth [^027-note1] heaven as a province of the same kingdom of Peace. Caused yt war to Cease between heaven and Earth which the Fall had also those wars and Contentions which were occasion'd, and war to Cease among the Inhabitants of the Earth

_____________

Doc. That the son of God by Appearing in Our Nature Laid a Glorious foundation for Peace to the Inhabitants of this World

___________________________

Here We shall Show Particularly how he hath laid a foundation for Peace 1. With God. 2. With Our selves & 3. With one Another I Peace With God. so dreadfull is the effect of the fall and of sin that it has made a breach between man and his Creator. the Almighty Jehovah. and dust and ashes are the Parties differing. In our man in his primitive state was a friend of God. God Dwel Dw Dwell'd then in this World and Used often to Converse with man and manifest himself to him. and as a Father and a friendly Correspondance and Intercourse was Maintain'd between heaven and Earth But Man has broke this friendship in that he has broke the Covenant that Was Made between God and Man. & broke the Command of God. and departed from his Allegiance with. heaven. Refuse Departed from his submission subjection to him as his sovereign. hereby man became An Enemy to God. his heart was fill'd with Enmity to him. his disposition Entirely Contrary to Gods, and all his Powers set in Opposition to him Rom 8 7 the Carnal mind is Enmity Against God and is not subject to the Law of God nor Indeed Can be. & hereby Gods displeasure was Justly Excited and his anger Incensed & hereby it Came to Pass that man was no Longer the object of Gods favour as he Used to be. but his Dreadfull frowns were Procured. and his displeasure Justly Incensed and man stood condemned to death. But By X Appearing in the World there is a foundation [^027-note2] for us, peace is Again Restored, and a foundation is Laid for An Ever Lasting friendship between God a friendship that is not Liable to be broken as the former was an alliance Can a a better and surer foundation. the foundation that it our friendship with heaven stood upon before was mans Free will but now it is innocency and Righteousness, but now it is the immutable Righteousness, and intercession of This Peace with God Consists in Gods being Reconciled un X Jesus /. to But us and in our being Reconciled unto God

____________________________________________________________

1 hereby God is Reconciled Unto us. X Doth this Reconciles

___________

1 By making satisfaction for sin. for tis upon the account of sin only that God is Angry with us, where sin is there Gods displeasure and hatred will be. God Cant be Reconciled unto sin. tho he may be Reconciled unto sinners. Wrath must be Executed Upon sin. till that be done God never will Reconciled to them that Committed it

Now the wrath of God is diverted from the head of the sinners and is executed upon the head of His beloved son of God Who Interposes himself stands in the Gap and bears all upon his own body and soul and shelters and secures us all the stormm lights on him and we Are sheltered and secured and Out of danger There is no more of Gods Wrath Remains twas all poured out on our Mediatour Who was Made sin for us. Now Who shall Lay Any thing to the Charge of Gods Elect i and Who is he that Condemneth Rom it is X that died Rom 8 33 34 no sacrifices or of X sacrifice of him self was of Infinite value his blood infinitely Precious. and altho all the offerings we Could offer bore no Can offer bear no Proportion at all to the offence yet that was Equal to it fully Equal to it and Enough Quite to make up the matter. he
