from his sacrifice was a savour Infinitely sweet to God and of Power sufficient to Appease Gods anger his anger and to Render him an he is so infinitely well Pleased with his son, that for his sake he is again well Pleased with all for whom he Undertook. God having an infinite love to X his own perfect Image and X having a dying love to the Elect his Wrath no longer subsists against the object of this Dying love. of his infinitely beloved 2 By Making Intercession. X having done all upon [^027-note3] Earth that God Required, and having fully accomplished the terms of the Covenant of Redemption, and finished all by his Death and Continuance in the Grave. he went into heaven to make Representation of what he had done before the throne of God. there is he Enters with his blood and shows his Wounds. and has this Plea to make for them that he had done all that God Required . John 17 4 I have finished the Work Which thou Gavest me to Do X Prays for sinners believers and What need they fear who have the Prayers of such a person Continually before the throne of Grace on their behalf. for God alwaies hears X Prayers John 11 42 and I knew that thou hearest me alwaies. Yea Xis Challenges and demands peace pardon & Reconciliation and he has Good Grounds for his Challenge a John 17 24 Father I will. and he has Good Ground for his Ple Challenge even Gods own promise that he made to him before the foundation of the World. Joh 17 6 thine they were and thou Gavest them me

Believers have Remainders of Sin that might and exercises of Corruption that might Justly be new provokations to God to Reject them and be their Enemy . but there is no danger of that as Long as they have so Powerfull an advocate in heaven. 1 Joh 2. 1 If any man sin we have An advocate With the Father. Jesus X the Righteous so that there is a upon a sinners Recieving X there is thenc e forward a settled and Everlasting Peace between God and God his soul. of which Jesus X is the Mediatour and therefore it Can never be Dissolved for tho the believer is often times transgressing and offending yet X who is his sponsor and answers for him never transgresses nor offends but is all alwaies wellpleasing to God both for himself both in himself and as Mediatour. .

__________________________________________________________

2. By X Coming into the World sinners Are Reconciled Unto God 1 he hath set before most Powerfull arguments to be Reconcciled to perswade us to be Reconciled to him. he hath made a more bright of his Glory. and shown us much more of his Excellency and beauty. for Which we have [^027-note4] the Greatest Reason to be no Longer Enemies to him but to If we Would not be Enemies to that being that is above all others amiable and lovely he has made known unto us more of his mercifull nature and of his Great Goodness and bounty. and particularly by him are set forth most astonishing Instances of his Grace towards us. to move upon to work and how that God has first sought Reconciliation with us. and tho we were Enemies, Yet has done a Great deal that we may be saved, and be happy to Work upon our Gratitude and Ingenuity. The disadvantageousness of this our war with heaven. on our side appears more Abundantly than before. if we Go On we must expect nothing but to be Overthrown with Everlasting Perdition. and forever to Endure the Wrath of Our Omnipotent adversary. and the advantage of Peace with God, the Everlasting Enjoyment of his favour and love and all Possible happiness. The terms of Reconciliation are Particularly decipher'd. are such as most Easy. Reasonable and honourable & Gracious not that we should Endure a long time of Pain, or Under go a Great deal of hardship. or perform any Cruel service but only to believe in the Name of Jesus X. accept of him and submit to him. & X is making proclamation of Peace unto us and Intreats us to be Reconciled and is sending his ministers 2 Cor 5 20

____________________________________________________________________________

2. X has Purchased mortification of that Enmity that is in us Against God, and that a new heart should be Given to us. Men Are all born with such a principle of Invete rate opposition Against God. that you may set before them What Arguments You Please Why they should be Re conciled they will still be Opposite till their Natures are Changed and they Are made new Creatures. But X has purchased Even this for us. and this God bestows through him Ezech 36 26 A new heart also Will I Give You and a New Spirit Will I Put Within You. and I will take away the stony heart I out of Your flesh and I will Give you and heart of flesh . & Jeremiah 31.31 32 33 behold the days Come saith the Lord that I will make a new [^027-note5] Covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah Not according to the Covenant I made With their Fathers &c But this shall be the Covenant that I will make With the house of Israel after those days saith the Lord. I will put my Law into their Inward Parts and Write it in their hearts and Will be their God and they shall be my People

________________________________________________________________

II C X has Laid foundation for Peace Within our selves sin has Put all things into an Uproar and Confusion in the mind hath set man at variance with himself. has made him his own Worst Enemy. in Whatever Circumstances he is the sinner is he has no peace, for there is Continuel war in his own breast, and he feels Great trouble and Uneasiness from the tumults and tempests that are in his own soul. tis X only that heals these divisions. and tis he Only that Can heal them. This Inward Peace Consists in two things 1 In the due subordination of the faculties and acts of the soul one to Another. sin has destroyed all order and Regularity in the Powers affections and exercises of the mind. Reason and Conscience Which God made to be or Rule are Pull'd down from the throne. and Cast in the dirt. & Passion and Carnal Appetites and sense. Usurp dominion & Tiranize in his heart and Govern the man. and he is Driven on to do those things that are Against Reason his Reason and the Natural suggestions of his own Understanding to he is hurried to do and to live in those things which his Reason tells him Are Rong wrong and Contrary to his own Interest and that will End in his misery. & Ruin. The most Excellent faculties are brought into Captivity to the basest affections and desires. now when it is things are in Confusion . as in a kingdom When in a kingdom the when the Noble and honourable are depress'd and Vilified. and the base and Vile have Rule. It is not likely that that kingdom in such will be in a. state of Peace. so it is in the soul of man When. Lo Wilfullness. & Pride, Lus [^027-note6] & anger domineer over the Noble Powers of Reason and Understanding, all will be in a state of Confusion and Contentions The spirit of X Regulates these things. he Restores order and thence follows Peace and tranquility. with the touch of his hand and Sprinkling of his blood. he allays all turbulent humours, and disorderly Passions of the mind and sets all to Rites in Calm and Quiet.

________________________

2 the Second Part of Inward Peace is Peace of Conscience the foregoing is Peace in the direct acts of the soul this in the Reflex. And Consists souls Uneasy and Painfull sense of its own Evil acts. in the Understandings Condemnation of them and foreboding Punishment. Tho we as man is fallen yet he is left with a natural sense in his own mind of Good and Evil so that moral Good will Appear amiable and moral Evil dreadfull deform'd and ill favourd. & that When he has Willfully done that wch is wrong and sinfull. when he Reflects upon it it will the sense of it will be Ungratefull and Painfull and excite a sort of horror & that fills the mind with a fearfull ness and Expectation of Punishment. he has an Inward intimation that he deserves Punishment and that he must expect it. it is a principle that all know the Very first time they Reflect on it that he that Does evil deserves evil. & therefore when he himself has Done Evil he Naturally expects that. Evil will befall him. and by how much the more Clear the light and knowledge is that men Enjoy. of God and his will and his Law and the sanctions of it, so much the Greater will these troublesome impressions of Uneasiness be from a sense of Guilt.

_____________________________________________

This Misery have We brought Upon our selves by sin we made our selves Guilty before God. and Our Own Reason and the Natural light that is in us. Condemns and Gives us to Expect the Wrath of that being that Governs the world. and we stand bound over by the sentence of our own Understandings to Punish the vengeance of God. It is a Very Great Calamity to Live with such an accusing [^027-note7] and Condemning Conscience. and such a fearfull sense of being displeasing to God. unreconciled to him. and oblig'dtion to Punishment from him. and sometimes especially the misery is very Great its a Continual hor horrour a fearfull sound, its sounds in mens Ears like like the dreadfull voice of God denouncing his wrath against them tho man he has no Peace nor Rest. but alwai he has no Quiet in his own breast but alwaies lives in fear of his life and his soul but X has set those that believe in him free from this Inward misery having fully satisfied Justice by his own sufferings and offerd a Sacrifice every way sufficient and Given Assurances to all that that Whosoever Comes to him he will Undertake for them. those Considerations set their minds at Ease are abundantly sufficient to Give Ease and Peace to and to lighten the mind of that heavy burden and set it free from that bondge it was held in. and to day do that which all the Ley gal sacrifices Could not do to make Perfect as to the Conscience. In him we may have the Comfortable Consideratione that God is Reconciled to us and is wellpleased with us that all our sins Are forgiven. we may behold his frowns turnd into smiles. and Wherever We Are, in Whatsoever Condition we may have the Comfort of thinking that we Are In the hands of a God that is at peace with us. that the he In Whose hand our breath is, in Whose hand our souls are, in Whose hand all our affairs are, and in whose hand all Creatures are, is not displeasd And Angry with us, but accepts us as wellpleasing in his sight.

____________________________________________________________

III X hath Laid Abundant foundation for Our Peace one With Another Tis the Nature and tendency of the Gospel of Jesus X to procure peace among men one with ano ther. Con strife and Contention. Malice. Envy. Debate. & mutual Ill will, are some of the Greatest miseries of this Apostate World. that which sets us at makes it most dif [^027-note8] ferent from heavenly, and most like to the Infernal world. and how has the Corruption that Reigns in mens hearts filld the World with these things; how Do mankind that Are made of the same blood and are Come of the same first father and mother devour and Persecute one Another. and with heart and hand Pu Work out one Anothers misery. surely tis a 'twould be a Glorious thing if God should send down some d Extraordinary messenger from heaven to the Earth to be a peacemaker amongst men. and to Reconcile them one to Another This hath God done he hath sent his own son on this Errand. and he hath Restores Peace to men these ways

1 he hath set a Wonderfull example of love and A & Peaceable spirit he Came into the World and descended from the heights of his Glory. out of love to man. Yea so great was his love that he Laid down his life for them. and that we may Plead as an excuse to Conten maintain Contention with men that they have Injured an and abused. X saved us Whilst we are si we were sinners. ## 52. Luke 2:14(b) 52.Luke 2'14b trans

Jonathan Edwards

Luke 2 14 ---- Good Will towards men Its Worthy of taking Notice of how the Angels seem to be Rejoiced at mans happiness. When X Appears in the World for mans salvation What a Rapture do they seem to be in about it and how full of Joy to see that Poor miserable and sinfull men are like to be saved from hell and to be brought into a state of favour With God Again. Those blessed spirits being full of love to God, Love all those that God loves loves that minister before his throne. being as it were swallowed up in love to God their king. Love all delight and Rejoice in the wellfare of all those that God Recieve in his Good Pleasure Recieves into his favour. and therefore tis, that With such Gladness upon X being born they with such Gladness they sing Peace on Earth & Good Will towards men. the same -------------------- as if they had said both Peace and Good will for men

___________________________

By Peace is only is Chiefly signified a meer Cessation of Gods displeasure. by Good will his Positive love and favour benevolence. By Gods being at Peace with men does not necessari Implies his forgiving of them and delivering them from Obligation to Punishment of & that Misery Which is the effect of his Anger. but dont Necessarily Includ Imply Any Positive love or favour. or any Intention of making them happy. but only of making not making them Miserable But this Latter expression signifies the exercise of his Positive his propensity and to their Good and Wellbeing. and Glorious design of their happiness By Good Will is the same thing as benevolence. Love is distin guished into a love of Complacence and a love of benevolence and a love of Complacence. Thus God loves the Elect while sinners and Enemies With a love of benevolence. that is he loves them with such a love as Inclines God to seek to their Wellfare and happiness. a love that seeks their Good he loves the Elect after Conversion With a love of Complacence that is he delights in them. for the sake of X. and delights in that beauty and excellency he has Given them Doc. That X Appearing In our Nature is an Instance [^028-note1] of Wonderfull love to man. Here

_______________________

1 We shall Enquire What is this love of God 2 We shall show What Love both the Father and the son have manifested hereby 3 shall show how Many Ways this Love of God was manifested by X in Our Nature. But

______________________

I What is this love of God Ans. Tis that Inclination to Communicate Goo Good ness & to Communicate blessedness, that is in the nature of God. Determin'd by his Wisdom and Good pleasure to some Particular objects. Tis Gods love of benevolence that we are now speaking of, we Observe that among Creature tis love that Inclines to Causes them to Desire and seek the Good of Another. Such an Inclinati on in men is Called love. and therefore that Inclination that is in the Nature of God to beneficence to do Good to Creatures is Called so too. tho indeed God is without Passions. be cause all Passions imply muta imutab Changeableness and Imperfection. and therefore Love Cant be in God as it is in us. because God an is a being infinitely Perfect. But Yet all that excellent and denotes perfection in the Love of Creatures, is in God more eminently in God in is in him In a transcendent and Infinite degree

______

But all that denotes Imperfection in love is not in God

__________________________

all that is in that Which we Call love. that is amiable & Obliges, and happy and Obliges the Object of it is in God so that we bent to Imagine that any thing of that which makes the Creatures love one to Another Appear Appear excellent and lovely to us. and Which engages our love to them is not in God for tis in him in the most exalted degree, and he is only without that which denotes mutability, passiveness and Ignorance.

As God is Infinitely happy in himself so there is such a thing [^028-note2] in the divine nature as a tendency or propensity to Communicate of himself and of his own happiness. not an Inclination not from any want in God or deficiency in God. But Rather from his I that he should stand in need of any other but from his Infinite fullness. and sufficiency Which doth as it were overflow to the Creature. Insuffi Goodness or an Inclination to Communicate happiness. much more Naturally argues. God a sufficiency and not a d Deficiency. for an Inf deficiency Rather Incline to Recieve than Communicate. dont Communicate because he has not our Enough for himself. but all sufficiency Communicates because he has more than Enough. Creatures often Love others from the Want they find in them selves that they may Recieve Good from them. but loves the Creature not that he may Recieve any thing from them. but Communicate to them Good to them. to Which Gods Infinitely Good and bountifull Nature Inclines him

_____

This Love And benevolence of God Dont extend it self equally to Every Creature. no not altho the Creatures be in themselves Every Way Equal. but is determin'd. By his In finite Wisdom, and his own Good Pleasure to some Particular objects, he Gives us no Other Reason, nor are we to Enquire after Any other. but the Why these and not others are beloved of God but because tis so is the Good Pleasure of his will. his Love is free, otherwise the Creature would not be Obliged to God for it and if it be free then God is at liberty to bestow it on Whom he Pleases, and to Withold it from Whom he Pleases Therefore it is not Any Consideration of loveliness or excellency in the Creature that Engages this love of God, but is Antecedent to all the excellency and Even to the very being of the Creature. and the motive of it is nothing but Gods own Good and Gracious Inclination. his natural propensity to Communicate himself and of the Infinite fullness of his own [^028-note3] happiness. Twas this love of God that moved God to Create the Creature and to make him excelent. his loveliness is an the effect of Gods love and therefore Cant be the foundation of it. Eph 1,4 According as he hath Chosen us in him before the foundation of the World 1 Joh 4 19 he loved us first.

______________

II X manifested in the flesh has made manifest both his Gl Father and his own Love. We Read of the Fathers love to Man and of the Love of the son, but not of the love of the holy Ghost. which seems to be because the holy Ghost is the Love of God it self. as the son is the essential wisdom of God- so the holy Ghost is the Essential love of God whereby he Infinitely loves himself. and Which love also overflows to Creatures. therefore he is Represented by a Dove Which is Used as the Emblem of Love in the scrip tures and by Profane Writers as the Emblem of love

_____________________

The love of the Father and the son towards man has different Modes. Arising from the different Relation Which they stand in Unto man in the affair of Redemption the Father sustains the Character of a Lawgiver unto man and therefore he is more directly the Person offended. and the Covenant was b Made between man and him, and therefore twas More Especially his Anger that was provoked, and him sin was Committed more Immediately Against him, and twas his Justice that Required satisfaction Therefore the Fathers Love appears in Giving his son in as it were in Parting With that that Infinitely dear to himself. and in admitting his satisfaction and Righteous for man. tho he was the Person offended, his Law Violated, his authority Contem trampled Under foot. Yet he Pitied man so under the misery had brought Upon himself by his Rebellion that he Gave so this Unde Unspeakeable Gift that he might, have a sufficient sacrifice to trust to for deliverance. & such was his benevolence that he Gave him to obey the Law for him. that [^028-note4] through him he might have Everlasting life.

________________________________

He sustaining the Character of a a Lawgiver. and so sustaining the Authority and Dignity of the Godhead. his love is a love of Clemency. manifested in Giving his son and in forgiving sin and Justifying and adopting sinners through him The son was Not Immediately offended by Mans sin. only but used only as he was Infinitely near to the Father and Partaker of the same divine Nature With him as as all sin is infinitely and alike Odious to all the Persons of the trinity. his Love therefore Appears in pitying men that had so violated the Law of his father Contemned his Authority and offended his Justice and was become so Odious a Creature by R sin. so as Place himself in his stead to & to suffer for and him and Perform a Righteousness for him. and by taking of them so near to himself and Uniting them to him in the same body. and Espousing of them to him. to be as their hus head and husband forever The Fathers Love is Remarkeable for this that he was the Person more directly offended by sin. and Yet loved him so as Give him so Great a Gift, the sons love is Remarkea ble for this that he Was the Person that Was to suffer and yet Loved man, and loved him Unto the Death. John 3 16 God so loved the World that he Gave his only begotten son. . 1 Joh 3 Chap 16. hereby Percieve we the love of God (that is God the son) that he laid Down his life for us

_____________________________________________________________

III We Are Come in the third Place to show how Many Ways this love of God to Man was Is manifested by X the son of God Incarnate 1 By his being in Our Nature. we Justly esteem it a wonderfull expression of Gods Grace that he will take Any no tice at all of so little and inferiour a thing as man. that he is treating With us, and Concern Reveals himself to us [^028-note5] and Concerns himself for us and About us. Psal 8.3 when I Consider thy heavens Which thou hast made the moon & stars ---------------- But this is visiting of us with a witness to become one of us. to Come down from heaven and take flesh and blood as Men have and Dwell among them for their Good If we Consider it it is Really a very strange thing that God should be man. not only wonderfully as to the manner of it s of the hypostaticall union. but strange that God should so much Concern himself about man that nature so distant should be United in one Person. that he that was Equal with God should become a servant have the form of a servant The love of God and X are appearing in this are wonderfull upon two Accounts. There is so much Condescension that the Eternal son of God would stoop to be In a finite Crooked Nature. and in so mean a Nature. not the Nature of seraphims that excell in strength but of weak man that dwells in a house of Clay. we speak of mans Nature now as it was in its primitive Perfectionn and then there is Great humiliation in it in that he took it With all those decays Ruins and Infirmities that sin had brought upon it tho he was without sin himself. Yet he Came into a world that was spoiled by sin and trod upon that Ground yt was Cursed. and took our nature with all those infirmities which sin had brought upon it except such as partook of the Nature of sin. his body was as liable to sickness & decays decays. & Corruption. and to be Injured by out as other mans tho he was a divine person Yea he did not only assumes mans Nature With those dishonours that Commo Universally attend it since the fall but in more mean Circum & low Circumstances than most men. he Want born in a kings Palace. but In a stable of an Obscure Virgin. Where the Cattle Used to bring forth their Young 2 By What he did in Our Nature. In Our Nature he [^028-note6] Obeyed the Law and Wrought Out a perfect Righteousness. If it be said that he was Obliged to Obey the Law. he & how was that a manifestation of love to us. I answer he was not Obliged to be made Under the Law. that was only on our account. he wa tho when he was man he was ob liged to Obey the Law of God Yet he was not Obliged to Obey it on Our Account to be our sponsor and Repres to Represent us, that was meerly from wonderfull love to us he not only subjec he was not only subject to the moral Law but the Ceremoni all. that heavy and burdensom Yoke of which the Apos tle says. that neither they nor their Fathers Were able to bear act Act 15.10 but this Yoke X Jesus wore he was Circumcised he attended their Passovers and festivals and all their Numerous forms and Ceremonies. That he might fulfill all Righteousness he Ob was subject to all the Laws Which God had Given to Man moral and Ceremonial. and tho he deliver'd others from this Yoke of bondage Yet he bore it himself he fullfilld the Ceremonial Law and then Abrogated it

he manifested his love to man by men by that Pains which he took in instructing of them. that he might deliver their minds from darkness that he Pitied them Under. how Industrious was he in Endeavouring to Lead men to the know ledge of saving truth taking all manner of opportunities to Instruct them. The Apostle in several of the foregoing Chapters had been Commending th to the Corinthians his ministry. to and h making profession of his Patience. diligence and faithfullness in the wor his work as an Apostle. to remove all prejudices that Otherwise might Arise against the Gospel which he Preached as tho he sought his own honour or private Interest in What he did. in the Latter part of the 5 Chapter he tells them that they Are sai even the apostles and ministers of X were Ambassadours were ambassadour for X those that th had the ministry of Reconciliation Committed to them and Appeard in X stead beseeching sinners to be Reconciled Unto God. And says the Apostle in the beginning of this Chapter we then as workers together with him beseech you also that ye Recieve not the Grace of God in Vain. that in that this t is that Gods Reconciling the World to himself by Jesus bent in vain as to you. we bes Labour Earnestly t as fellow workers with X as those that Are Carrying on the same design of Reconciling the world unto God, we Labour Earnestly that what X has done maynt in order to Your Reconciliation maynt be in vain. This is Our Workand says he in the 3d verse we Labour to Give no off [^033-note1] offence in any thing. that in but in all things Approving our selves as the ministers of God that the ministry be not blamed. that is we Endeavour to the Utmost so to behave Our selves so as to Give no Prejudice none should take any Prejudice Against the Gospel by Our be haviour. but acting so that Every one may see that we live as becomes the ministers and Ambassadours of X. And this he did these ways as he says in the 4 a 5 & 6 verses. By behaving himself with much Patience, in aff lictions and Persecutions. & by Purely Pureness of life that is by keeping himself free from all dishonesty. Intemperance or Lasciviousness and all manner of filthy Conversation. and by knowledge that is by behaving himself Prudently and Understandingly. and by Long suffering. that is by being meek and patient towards those that Abused and Injured him. by kindness__ to all by being Ready at all times to help and benefit and promote the benefit of all. by the holy Ghost a by showi that is by showing the fruits of Gods spirit in his Conversation. by Love Unfeigned, that is without secretly desig hypocrisie or secretly designing mischief their hurt or Only Intending his own Good. By the word of truth, for the truth of God Recommends it self and Carries [^033-note2] its own light with it by the Power of God. that that is in working of miracles or spirtual wonders in mens hearts & Lastly by the Armour of Righteousness on the Right hand and on the Left that is the which is that is the Gifts and Graces of Gods spirit which Are the weapons of a Xtians warfare. Thus the Apostle behaved himself that by such a behaviour he might Recommend the message he brought.. That he Goes on in the 8.9 & 10 verses to tell in What Circumstances he thus behaved himself in honour and dishonour in Evil Report and Good Report. wh when I was C when Counted a deciever. tho Indeed I am true. a when treated as Unknown as a stranger, yet well known. as dying for I am and behold we alive, that is in the Continual dangers of death I am in tho I am alive still. as Chastend yet not killed. when the life of the life of my body and is wonderfully Preserved by God. or tho my outward man was it was killed yet my day dies dayly yet my Inward man lives as Chastend yet not killed. In the midst of all mens Cruelties yet my life is Preserved I am neither dead nor discouraged. As sorrowfull yet alwaies Rejoicing I meet with many outward Calamities sorrows yet I have Abundance of spiritual Joy and Comfort. as poor Yet making many [^033-note3] Rich, poor as to Outward things yet making many Rich in spiritual things . & Lastly as having nothing and Yet Possessing all things which may be understood as Including both these. ei
